title: Integration assumption for deferred stable-staker M-05 wiring: caller MUST pay-out/write-off principal to its end user BEFORE calling relinquishPrincipal and MUST NOT re-credit the resulting reflax surplus to the same owner (else cross-protocol double-count)
function: relinquishPrincipal (primitive staged ahead of its consumer — no stable-staker callsite exists at this commit)

crossReference.note: Binds to the deferred stable-staker M-05 (valid Medium, owner-accepted, pro-rata-haircut fix DEFERRED pending exactly this reflax relinquishPrincipal story — per MEMORY stable-staker-m05-fix-pending-vault notes).

description: relinquishPrincipal is a primitive staged ahead of its consumer; there is currently NO callsite in stable-staker at this commit (2f6774d). The reflax-side write-down releases the backing vault value as surplus to remaining clients. IF a future stable-staker caller both (a) fails to pay-out/write-off the principal to its end user before relinquishing AND (b) re-credits the resulting reflax surplus to the same owner, the same value is counted on both sides of the integration (cross-protocol double-count). Distinct from existing spec-conformance entries F-01 (provable-solvency overstated) and F-02 (IYieldStrategy NatSpec staleness) — different subject: cross-protocol integration, not solvency rounding or doc staleness.
impact: Potential cross-protocol double-count of principal IF a future stable-staker caller credits the reflax surplus to the same owner whose principal it already paid out/wrote off. No current asset impact: the primitive is staged ahead of its consumer and no callsite exists. Filing at H/M now would be 'speculation on future code without demonstrated root cause' (explicitly known-invalid per CLAUDE.md), so it is recorded as a forward-looking spec-conformance / integration constraint, visible to the owner.
attackPath: 1. (Future, hypothetical — no callsite today) stable-staker wires relinquishPrincipal as the reflax-side of its deferred M-05 pro-rata-haircut fix.

2. If that wiring relinquishes principal WITHOUT first paying-out/writing-off the principal to the end user, OR re-credits the freed reflax surplus to the same owner, the same value is counted on both sides of the integration.
3. This would surface as a value mis-statement at the stable-staker boundary — but only once the constraint is actually violated by real wiring.
lawBasis: Law-2 cross-protocol faithfulness/integration constraint. Recorded (not dropped) per Law-1 so the constraint is audited when the wiring lands. Tagged faithfulness:true and routed to the spec-conformance channel (NOT buried in the QA/gas bundle).
documentationCheck: NOT-A-KNOWN-ISSUE and not suppressible. knownIssuesCount=0; no designDecision or systemAssumption documents a cross-protocol double-count guard.

reEvaluation.trigger: the stable-staker relinquishPrincipal caller wiring lands AND violates the pay-out-then-relinquish / no-double-credit constraint
reEvaluation.reEvaluateAt: Medium severity at the stable-staker integration point (a cross-protocol value double-count is value-leak-with-stated-assumptions territory)

recommendation: Record in spec-conformance.md, bound to deferred stable-staker M-05. When stable-staker wires relinquishPrincipal: assert the caller pays-out/writes-off principal to the end user BEFORE relinquishing, and does NOT re-credit the reflax surplus to the same owner. Re-evaluate at Medium severity at that integration point.
report: spec-conformance.md (Law-2 cross-protocol integration channel; NOT the QA bundle)
